subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Crank-Rocker: One Spins, One Rocks
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Crank-Rocker: One Spins, One Rocks usable.

hook.text: One link spins continuously. The opposite link swings back and forth.

buildup.text: The shortest link is the crank. It rotates fully while the rocker oscillates.

discovery.text: This converts steady rotation into a back-and-forth sweep of any angle.

twist.text: The rocker spends more time going one way than the other. It's not symmetric.

climax.text: Windshield wipers use a crank-rocker to sweep across the glass.

punchline.text: Spin the crank and the rocker does the waving.

quiz.question: Why does a crank-rocker produce unequal forward and return times?
options: The motor speeds up and slows down during each revolution
The geometry creates unequal angular travel for forward and return strokes
Friction slows the rocker on the return swing
